look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Turn a middle leaf over and find the row of stiff prickles along the underside midrib. Inspect clasping auriculate leaf bases and small narrow yellow-flowered heads; milky sap on a fresh break.
taxonomy_notes: Accepted species Lactuca serriola L. in Kew; Lactuca scariola and Lactuca sativa subsp. serriola are synonyms/alternative treatments, not separate cards.

project_inclusion.source_pool: Master Plant Pool row 613; installer preflight mass-05
project_inclusion.notes: Kew Old World native range, introduced in North America; no invasive claim.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect annual or biennial herb, leafy stem branching above, milky sap.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Alternate variable lobed gray-green leaves, clasping auricles and underside midrib row of spines.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Narrow cylindrical heads with small yellow strap-shaped ligulate florets.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Beaked flattened cypsela with white pappus; macro still needed.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Stems often glabrous to prickly; milky latex.

confused_with: Sonchus asper: glossy, spiny-margined clasping leaves; compare underside midrib and heads.
Lactuca canadensis: check underside midrib prickles, leaf bases and fruit.
Lactuca virosa: close look-alike; compare mature fruit and leaves.
comparisons.key_distinctions: Row of stiff spines along abaxial leaf midrib plus clasping auricles, milky latex and narrow yellow ligulate heads.
